newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Cotton prices seen mixed in India, Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Cotton prices seen mixed in India, Pakistan.

text.p: Cotton prices were likely to remain mixed in India and Pakistan in the next week, dealers in the two countries said on Thursday.
Indian prices recovered on continued buying by state firms while Pakistani prices eased owing to a shortage of funds.
A dealer in India said, "initially mill buying was low but continued purchases by the state-owned agencies and particularly the Cotton Corporation of India dragged prices upward."
Later, millers were active buyers, helping the fresh gains.

In spot deals, Bengal-deshi rose five rupees to 840/865 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned moved up 10/20 rupees to 1,410/1,630 rupees. Punjab F-414 rose five to 1,825/1,850 rupees per maund.
Gujarat Sankar-4 (long-staple) climbed 300/500 rupees to 17,000/17,500 per candy (355.56 kg) for the average variety and the superior variety was quoted at 18,500/19,000 rupees.

"The government has so far allowed export of more than one million bales (170-kg) of cotton for the current cotton season and the market has seen continued overseas support," said Manubhai Amarsey, a leading dealer.
"Even spinning mills also remained active buyers amid increased overseas demand for cotton yarn," he said.
New crop arrivals at producing centres fell due to severe cold and farmers' festive mood for the kite festival on January 14, dealers said.
"I expect arrivals to pick up in the coming days," Amarsey said.
In Pakistan, prices are likely to remain mixed for several reasons including a shortfall of about one million 375-lb ginned bales from a poor crop and low buying by spinners, dealers said.
Spinners face a shortage of funds as they have used their sanctioned loan limits due to high domestic prices, dealer Nasim Usman said.
He said prices were now likely to fall on slow buying by spinners due to lack of yarn orders from abroad.
Government officials saw cotton production at nine million bales with the spinning industry expected to use 8.5 to 9.0 million bales.

Cotton arrivals at ginneries by January 2 were 7.4 million bales compared to 7.7 million lasr year, an official said. Arrivals in Punjab were 5.6 million bales and in Sindh 1.8 million against 6.3 million and 1.4 million respectively.

Of total ginned cotton mills had bought 5.5 million bales compared to 5.3 million in the year-ago period, he said. Unsold stocks with ginneries were 1.9 million bales compared to 1.7 million in the same period last year.
The main reason for unsold stocks was a credit squeeze that became effective after December 1, the official said.
On the kerb, MNH-93 was 2,350 to 2,360 rupees per maund, a Karachi Cotton Association broker said.
